text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD
- The Interior Ministry is alarmed by a growing number of international fraud organisations working in Austria.
- Chancellor Viktor Klima has announced a new initiative to increase the number of apprenticeships.
- Chemicals giant Novartis plans to extend its research facilities in Austria, making Vienna its centre for research on skin diseases.
- Federal grid company Verbund has criticised Economics Minister Hannes Farnleitner's plans to liberalise Austria's energy market.
- Oil and chemicals group OMV and provincial energy provider EVN will discuss a joint participation in provincial gas company Begas.
- The number of insolvencies in Austria went up 14 percent in 1996, the third-highest increase within the European Union.
- Andreas Treichl has been nominated as new chief executive of Die Erste savings bank. Talks over taking over Bank Austria's stake in GiroCredit are coming to an end.
DIE PRESSE
- Austria's government has agreed to pay 25,000 schillings to every Bosnian refugee who is willing to return to his home country.
- Austria will change weekly motorway fees as a result of German protests.
- Wages and the savings quota will fall while the unemployment rate will rise as the government's austerity measures take their toll, research institute IHS expects.
- Austria's central bank will loose billions of schillings when European Monetary Union is introduced, as the European Central Bank will pay its profits according to a special system.
KURIER
- Vienna is Austria's only state to have greatly increased the number of nationalisations. All the other states have had a major decrease in the number of nationalisations.
SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN
- Stationer Libro plans to extend its activities abroad after investor UIAG takes over the company and its subsequent listing on Vienna's stock exchange.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- Demand for Creditanstalt shares has grown after its price had fallen after Bank Austria's takeover of the bank.
- While Die Erste savings bank takeover of the majority in GiroCredit is expected to be fixed, the savings banks' union's blocking minority is still insecure.
